title: The restless mind and the seeker who falls short

verses.sa: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥
verses.tr: Thus, the disciplined yogi, free from impurity, always unites the self with the supreme reality and attains limitless joy through that contact.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna after having described how the mind settles and the highest joy is found. He now explains the condition of the yogi who has reached that state.

body.text: Thus, the disciplined yogi, free from impurity, always unites the self with the supreme reality and attains limitless joy through that contact. The word yogi here means one who unites, and the word vitakalmasah means free from impurity. It is the yogi who is free from impurity who attains that limitless joy. Krishna then explains that this yogi sees the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self.

verses.sa: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
verses.tr: The one united in yoga sees the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, seeing everything with equal vision.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues the teaching on the inner vision of the meditator, moving from the quiet mind to the way that mind sees the world.

body.text: The one united in yoga sees the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, seeing everything with equal vision. The verse turns on two words, sarvabhutastham and atmani. The yogi sees the self situated in all beings, and all beings situated in the self. It is the same self, the same beings, held in one gaze. Krishna now asks who truly sees him, and he answers with the same equal vision.

verses.sa: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.tr: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me.
verses.angle: pranasyaami: the promise of never being lost
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What happens to a person who truly sees the divine in every living thing? Krishna answers with a promise of unbreakable closeness.

body.text: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me. The word pranasyaami means to disappear or be lost. Krishna says he will never disappear from the yogi's sight, and the yogi will never disappear from his. Krishna then says this united yogi lives in him and acts in the world without losing that vision. Listen to verse thirty-one.

verses.sa: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
verses.tr: The yogi who abides in unity and worships Me in all beings lives in Me, even while acting in every way.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just taught Arjuna to see the divine in every being. Now he describes what happens to a person who truly lives in that unity.

body.text: The yogi who abides in unity and worships Me in all beings lives in Me, even while acting in every way. Here is the word vartate, abides. It means the yogi is rooted inside Krishna, even while doing everyday tasks. Krishna then calls out to Arjuna to hear the highest standard of yoga.

verses.sa: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, the yogi who sees all beings as equal through the measure of the true self, and sees pleasure and pain alike, is considered the highest yogi.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the inner test of a true meditator. Listen for how he pairs pleasure with pain.

body.text: O Arjuna, the yogi who sees all beings as equal through the measure of the true self, and sees pleasure and pain alike, is considered the highest yogi. The word samam, equally, is the hinge of this verse, showing that the highest yogi does not favor pleasure over pain. Arjuna immediately doubts that anyone can keep a steady mind when it is so restless.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Krishna, you have described this yoga as balanced, but I do not see its steady practice, because the mind is restless.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just heard Krishna praise the highest yogi, the one who sees all beings as equal. Listen to how Arjuna responds to that ideal.

body.text: Arjuna says: Krishna, you have described this yoga as balanced, but I do not see its steady practice, because the mind is restless. Arjuna addresses Krishna as Madhusudana, the slayer of the demon Madhu, and then admits that because of his restless mind, he simply cannot see how to keep such a steady state. He admits that controlling this turbulent mind is as hard as taming the wind.

verses.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verses.tr: The mind is restless, turbulent, stubborn, and strong. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.
verses.angle: Pramathi: the word that means churning
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna carries on from his last complaint, naming the four qualities of the mind that make it so hard to master.

body.text: The mind is restless, turbulent, stubborn, and strong. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind. Listen to one word, pramathi. It means churning, and it shows how the mind agitates the body and the senses until they are restless. Krishna answers that the mind is hard to tame, but it can be mastered through practice and detachment.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
verses.tr: The mind is hard to control, but it is mastered through practice and detachment.
verses.angle: Abhyasa and vairagya master the mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just said controlling the mind is as hard as controlling the wind. What does Krishna say is possible instead?

body.text: The mind is hard to control, but it is mastered through practice and detachment. Krishna does not argue with Arjuna here. He agrees the mind is restless and hard to restrain, then names the two tools that master it: practice and detachment. He now explains that yoga is hard to reach without this control, but possible for the one who strives.

verses.sa: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥
verses.tr: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose mind is not fully controlled. But for one who controls the mind and strives with the right method, it can be reached.
verses.angle: The word yogah is the subject
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks plainly to Arjuna about the conditions that make yoga either impossible or possible. Listen to the two kinds of people he describes.

body.text: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose mind is not fully controlled. But for one who controls the mind and strives with the right method, it can be reached. Listen to the word yogah. It is the subject of the whole verse. Krishna is not talking about a posture, but about the very state of union, and he says it is hard to attain for the uncontrolled mind. Arjuna asks what happens to the person who begins with faith but then turns away before reaching the goal.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: What happens to a person who has faith but lacks steady effort, whose mind turns away from yoga before full success is reached, O Krishna?
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna now asks about a different kind of traveler on the path, one who begins with faith but loses his footing. Listen for how he names this state.

body.text: Arjuna says: What happens to a person who has faith but lacks steady effort, whose mind turns away from yoga before full success is reached, O Krishna? The key word here is ApAya, which means without attaining. Arjuna is asking what becomes of a person who fails to attain yoga-siddhi. He is not asking about the faithless, but the sincere one who falls short, and he wants to know if that effort is lost. Next, Arjuna continues.

verses.sa: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
verses.tr: O mighty-armed one, does a person who has fallen from both sides, like a torn cloud, perish without support, deluded on the path of the supreme reality?
verses.angle: Torn cloud: a failed yogi with no support
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has already asked what happens to someone who starts the spiritual path but loses faith before success. Now he asks a darker question.

body.text: O mighty-armed one, does a person who has fallen from both sides, like a torn cloud, perish without support, deluded on the path of the supreme reality? Arjuna uses a single image, a torn cloud. He asks what becomes of a person who loses support in both the world and on the path to liberation, left floating and scattered in the sky. Next, Arjuna continues.

verses.sa: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
verses.tr: O Krishna, only you can fully cut away this doubt. No one else is able to remove it.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks Krishna to cut his doubt completely
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just asked about the fate of a seeker who falls from the path, and now he admits he cannot resolve this alone.

body.text: O Krishna, only you can fully cut away this doubt. No one else is able to remove it. Arjuna tells Krishna that no one else is able to remove this doubt; he is not asking for an answer he can find with his own mind, but for a complete cutting away that only Krishna can provide. Krishna answers that such a person finds no destruction either here or hereafter.
